Lano: Probably a short form of names like Lano or Gaelano, or a modern coined name. Origin uncertain.
Léni: Short form of Leonie, Helene or Leonhard; from Latin leo 'lion' or Greek helene.
Saifeddine: Arabic Sayf al-Din, 'sword of the faith'.
Salem: Arabic and Hebrew, 'peace' or 'safe', from the root s-l-m.
Alexio: Italian and Spanish-style variant of Alexis, from Greek alexein, 'to defend'.
Cheick: West African French spelling of Arabic sheikh, 'elder' or 'leader'.
Even: Norwegian, from Old Norse Eyvindr, 'island wind' or 'good fortune'. Also Hebrew 'stone'.
Francisca: Portuguese, Spanish and Dutch feminine of Franciscus, 'Frenchman' or 'free one'.
Jazz: From the music genre, whose origin is uncertain. Used as a modern given name.
Kalvin: Variant spelling of Calvin, from French chauve 'bald', via Jean Calvin.
Kamille: French and Danish form of Camille, from Latin camillus, a young ritual attendant.
Mikolaj: Polish Mikołaj, form of Nicholas, from Greek nike 'victory' and laos 'people'.
Nisse: Scandinavian short form of Nils, from Nicholas, Greek 'victory of the people'. Also a Nordic household gnome.
Noélyne: French, a feminine form of Noël, from Latin natalis, 'birthday', meaning Christmas.
Precious: English virtue name from Old French precios, 'of great value'.
Yehuda: Hebrew form of Judah, 'praised'. Biblical son of Jacob.
Alessa: Italian and German short form of Alessandra, from Greek Alexandros, 'defender of men'.
Charlise: Modern English blend of Charlene or Charlotte and Lise, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Daniya: Arabic, 'near' or 'close'; also a Slavic or Hebrew variant of Daniel.
Diar: Kurdish and Arabic; possibly 'home' or 'homeland', from Arabic dar. Uncertain.
Lauke: Frisian and Dutch diminutive of Laurens, from Latin Laurentius, 'of Laurentum' or 'laurelled'.
Maxent: French, from Latin Maxentius, derived from Maximus, 'greatest'.
Niyo: Probably a modern coined name, possibly Japanese or African in origin. Origin uncertain.
Ritaje: Arabic Ritaj, 'closed gate' or 'door'. In Arabic, ritaj also denotes a locked gate.
Rolf: Scandinavian and German short form of Rudolf, from hrod 'fame' and wulf 'wolf'.
Sheldon: English place-name surname from Old English scelf 'ledge' and dun 'hill'.
Harone: Probably a variant of Aaron or Haron, from Hebrew Aharon, of uncertain meaning. Origin uncertain.
Kali: Sanskrit, 'black' or 'time', a Hindu goddess. Also Greek kali 'beautiful'.
Lexx: Modern spelling variant of Lex, a short form of Alexander, Greek 'defender of men'.
Mahault: Old French form of Matilda, from Germanic maht 'might' and hild 'battle'.
Marcelina: Spanish, Polish and Portuguese feminine of Marcelino, a diminutive of Marcus, perhaps 'of Mars'.
Maysam: Arabic, from maysam 'smiling' or 'beautiful face'. Also Persian 'beautiful face'.
Mikaela: Feminine form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Nane: Short form of Nanette, Johanna or Nana; or an Armenian girl's name for 'mother'. Origin uncertain.
Nyna: Variant of Nina, a Russian short form of names like Antonina, or Spanish niña 'girl'.
Shayma: Arabic Shayma, 'beauty mark' or 'having a mole'; also borne by the Prophet's foster sister.
Züleyha: Turkish form of Zulaikha, the wife of Potiphar in Islamic tradition; Arabic 'fair' or 'brilliant'.
Amon: Egyptian god Amun, 'hidden'. Also a Hebrew variant meaning 'faithful' or 'builder'.
Duarte: Portuguese form of Edward, from Old English ead 'wealth' and weard 'guard'.
Esil: Turkish Esil or Kazakh, from Esil 'river'. Possibly a variant of Esra. Origin uncertain.
Iga: Polish short form of Agnieszka, from Greek hagne 'pure', or of Jadwiga. Also Japanese place name.
Jip: Dutch, a diminutive of Jan or a nickname 'Jip' from the children's books Jip and Janneke.
Meryl: English, a variant of Muriel, from Celtic 'sea-bright'. Made famous by Meryl Streep.
Mo: Short form of Mohammed (Arabic 'praised') or Maurice, Moritz or Maureen.
Alessya: Modern spelling of Alessia, feminine of Alessio, from Greek alexein, 'to defend'.
Daylano: Modern coined name, perhaps blending Dylan or Dayan and Lano. Origin uncertain.
Edan: Irish Aedán, 'little fire'. Also Hebrew eden 'delight'.
Jullian: Variant of Julian, from Latin Julianus, 'belonging to Julius'.
Katalina: Spanish and Basque form of Catherine, from Greek, probably 'pure'.
Loreana: Modern blend of Lorena and Ana. Lorena is from Lorraine, from Germanic Lothar.
Lysandre: French form of Lysander, from Greek lysis 'release' and andros 'of man'. 'Liberator'.
Mattys: Dutch variant of Matthijs, the Dutch form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Sieme: Frisian, a variant of Siemen or Sieme from Germanic sigi 'victory'; also a Dutch diminutive of Simon. Uncertain.
Tiano: Short form of Christiano or Sebastiano. Origin uncertain.
Aina: Catalan and Hawaiian use; in Arabic 'eyes'; in Catalan a form of Anna. Meaning depends on culture.
Amauri: French form of Amalric, Germanic amal 'work' and ric 'ruler'.
Annabella: Latin-style blend of Anna and Bella, 'grace' and 'beautiful'.
Charel: Luxembourgish form of Charles, from Germanic karl, 'free man'.
Dylana: Feminine of Dylan, a Welsh name probably meaning 'son of the sea'.
Fae: English variant of Fay, 'fairy', from Old French fae. Also a short form of Faith.
Lianna: Probably a blend of Lia and Anna, or from French lier 'to bind'. Origin uncertain.
Lizie: Diminutive of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Wanis: Arabic Wanis, 'friendly' or 'companionable'. Also a short form of Wannes.
Adham: Arabic, 'black' or 'dark'. Also a Sufi name from Ibrahim ibn Adham.
Erol: Turkish, from er 'man' and ol 'be', 'be brave'.
Fedde: Frisian, a short form of Frederik or Fredde, from Germanic fridu 'peace' and ric 'ruler'.
Inoa: Probably a modern coined name or from Hawaiian inoa, 'name'.
Martyna: Polish and Czech feminine of Martin, from Latin Martinus, 'of Mars'.
Salvador: Spanish and Portuguese, 'saviour', from Latin salvator.
Sohail: Arabic Suhayl, the star Canopus; also 'smooth, easy' in Arabic.
Tanaïs: Greek Tanais, the ancient name of the Don river. In French use, a rare feminine name.
War: Dutch short form of Warner or Wouter; or from Belgian Limburg. Origin uncertain.
Zilan: Kurdish, a place name and a girl's name; also a Turkish name after the Zilan valley.
Aedan: Irish Aodhán, a diminutive of Aodh 'fire'. Variant of Aidan.
Alican: Turkish, from Ali (Arabic 'high' or 'noble') and can 'soul' or 'life'.
Camilo: Spanish and Portuguese form of Camillus, from Latin camillus, a young attendant.
Charle: Variant of Charles, from Germanic karl, 'free man'.
Erick: Variant of Eric, from Old Norse Eirikr, 'ever ruler'.
Hadija: Variant of Khadija, Arabic 'premature baby'. Name of the Prophet Muhammad's first wife.
Inora: Probably a coined name, perhaps linked to Honora or Eleanor. Origin uncertain.
Kyaro: Probably a modern coined name; possibly Japanese kyaro. Origin uncertain.
Lincoln: English place-name surname from Roman Lindum Colonia. Made famous by Abraham Lincoln.
Liselore: Dutch, a blend of Lise (Elisabeth) and Lore (Eleonore or Laura).
Liss: Short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Also Welsh 'court'.
Mylena: Variant of Milena, Slavic mil 'dear, gracious'. Also a Greek-style blend.
Nim: Probably a short form of Nimrod or Nimue; Dutch short form of Nimwegen. Origin uncertain.
Rinad: Probably a variant of Renata or Rinat, or Tatar Rinat. Origin uncertain.
Tessia: Probably a variant of Tessa or Theresia, from Greek therizein 'to harvest' or 'summer'. Origin uncertain.
Anays: Catalan and Spanish form of Anaïs, Occitan form of Anna, 'grace'.
Bailey: English surname from Old French baillis, 'bailiff' or 'steward'.
Brayden: Modern English coinage from the surname Braden, probably Irish 'salmon'.
Elicia: Variant of Alicia, from Germanic Adalheid, 'noble kind'.
Evangeline: From Greek euangelion, 'good news'. Popularised by Longfellow's 1847 poem.
Ewa: Polish form of Eve, from Hebrew chavah, 'life'.
Fre: Dutch or Frisian short form of Frederik, from Germanic fridu 'peace' and ric 'ruler'.
Joaquín: Spanish form of Joachim, from Hebrew 'God will establish'.
Kais: Arabic Qays, 'firm' or 'strong'. Also a Frisian short form.
Kamelya: Turkish for the camellia flower, named after the Jesuit Georg Kamel.
Ksawery: Polish form of Xavier, from Basque etxe berri 'new house'.
Lupe: Spanish short form of Guadalupe, from Arabic wadi 'valley' and Latin lupus 'wolf'.
Lyandro: Variant of Leandro, from Greek leon 'lion' and aner 'man'.
Léopoldine: French feminine of Léopold, from Germanic leud 'people' and bald 'bold'.
Siri: Scandinavian short form of Sigrid, 'beautiful victory'. Also Sanskrit 'splendour'.
Solyne: French, possibly a variant of Solène or Soline, from Latin solemnis. Origin uncertain.
Annaelle: French, a blend of Anna and Elle, or a variant of Anne-Elle. Anna is Hebrew 'grace'.
Ariadne: Greek, 'most holy'. Daughter of King Minos who helped Theseus in the labyrinth.
Daouda: West African form of Dawud, Arabic for David, 'beloved'.
Demian: Variant of Damian, from Greek damazein, 'to tame'.
Doutzen: Frisian, a diminutive of Douwe 'dove' or Dutch name; known from model Doutzen Kroes. Origin uncertain.
Eliseo: Italian and Spanish form of Elisha, Hebrew 'God is salvation'.
Ledion: Albanian, perhaps from Greek. Possibly 'lion'. Origin uncertain.
Maily: Modern coinage, probably a variant of Mailys or Mayley. Origin uncertain.
Mylla: Probably a variant of Milla or Mila, Slavic 'dear, gracious'. Origin uncertain.
Pina: Italian short form of Giuseppina, Hebrew 'God will add'. Also Spanish 'pine' and Hindi.
Stanislaw: Polish Stanisław, from Slavic stani 'to become' and slava 'glory'.
Danial: Arabic and Persian form of Daniel, Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Dexter: English, 'dyer' from Old English, or Latin dexter 'right-handed, skilled'.
Emmylou: American compound of Emmy and Lou. Made known by singer Emmylou Harris.
Isac: Portuguese and Swedish form of Isaac, from Hebrew 'he will laugh'.
Izzie: English diminutive of Isabel or Isidora, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Kamilya: Variant of Kamilia or Kamila, from Latin camillus, and Arabic Kamila 'perfect'.
Kayne: Modern English coinage, possibly from Kane, Irish Cathán 'battle', or Hawaiian 'man'.
Keylan: Modern coined name, perhaps a blend of Kai and Dylan or Kylan. Origin uncertain.
Sloan: Anglicised Irish surname Ó Sluaghadháin, 'descendant of the raider'.
Suzana: Slavic and Romanian form of Susanna, from Hebrew shoshannah, 'lily'.
Trevor: Welsh place-name surname, from tref 'homestead' and fawr 'large'.
Aléna: Czech and Slovak Alena, a form of Helena, probably 'torch'. Also a Slavic name.
Christ: From Greek Christos, 'anointed'. As a given name, a short form of Christiaan or Christophe.
Eluna: Modern coined name, perhaps from Luna 'moon' or Elena. Origin uncertain.
Eléonora: Italian, Greek and Eastern European form of Eleanor, possibly linked to Helen.
Fallon: Irish surname Ó Fallamhain, 'descendant of Fallamhan' ('leader'). Modern given name.
Kiyana: Modern name, probably from Persian Kiana, 'royal'; also an African American coinage.
Lowik: Frisian and Dutch form of Lodewijk, Louis. Germanic hlud 'famous' and wig 'battle'.
Matto: Italian short form of Matteo; also Lakota 'bear'. Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Mihail: Romanian and Bulgarian form of Michael, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Oana: Romanian form of Joan or Ioana, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'.
Olympia: Greek, 'of Olympus', the home of the gods. Also a Greek city.
Penélope: Spanish and French form of Penelope, Greek, possibly 'weaver' (pene 'thread'). Wife of Odysseus.
Rubén: Spanish form of Reuben, Hebrew 'behold, a son'.
Aleksi: Finnish form of Alexis, from Greek alexein, 'to defend'.
Djenabou: West African, from Arabic Zaynab, 'fragrant tree'. Fulani form.
Graziano: Italian form of Gratian, from Latin gratus, 'pleasing'.
Loe: Short form of Chloe, Eloise or Loes. Greek chloe 'green shoot'.
Loyd: Variant spelling of Lloyd, from Welsh llwyd, 'grey'.
Maggie: English diminutive of Margaret, from Greek margarites, 'pearl'.
Miron: Slavic form of Myron, from Greek myron 'fragrant oil'. Also Hebrew 'my peace'.
Nevio: Italian, from Latin Naevius, a Roman family name, 'mole' or 'birthmark'.
Saliou: West African form of Salih, Arabic 'righteous'. Wolof usage.
Thorin: From Old Norse Thorinn, 'bold', and Thor. Name of Tolkien's dwarf king.
Yvana: Variant of Ivana, the Slavic feminine of Ivan, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Aila: Finnish; also Arabic Ayla 'moonlight' and Scottish Ailsa. Meaning varies by culture.
Artus: French form of Arthur, Celtic perhaps 'bear' or 'stone'.
Elisabeta: Romanian, Bulgarian form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Gohan: Japanese gohan, 'cooked rice' or 'meal'. Used from the Dragon Ball character.
Lean: Probably a Dutch short form of Leander, from Greek 'lion man'. Or an English name 'thin'.
Libby: English diminutive of Elizabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Loek: Dutch diminutive of Lodewijk or Lukas. Germanic 'famous battle' or Greek 'from Lucania'.
Lucenzo: Probably a variant of Lorenzo or Lucenzo, from Latin Laurentius or lux 'light'. Origin uncertain.
Lyzéa: Modern coined name, possibly from Lysée or Elisa. Origin uncertain.
Mailo: Modern name, probably of Danish or Spanish origin, perhaps from Milo or Maylo. Origin uncertain.
Millan: Spanish form of Emilian, from Latin Aemilianus, from Aemilius 'rival'.
Mirabelle: French, from Latin mirabilis, 'wonderful'. Also a plum variety.
Nanne: Frisian and Scandinavian short form of Johanna or Anne; Dutch masculine also. 'Grace'.
Norma: Latin norma, 'rule' or 'pattern'. Bellini opera of 1831.
Solena: Breton and French, from Latin solemnis, 'solemn', or from Saint Solenne. Probably also linked to sol 'sun'.
Tigran: Armenian, from Old Persian, perhaps 'fierce'. Name of Tigranes the Great.
Yaelle: French spelling of Hebrew Yael, 'mountain goat' or 'ibex'.
Amylia: Variant of Amelia, from Germanic amal 'work', or of Aemilia.
Chems: Arabic Shams, 'sun'. Short form of Chemseddine.
Enéa: Italian and French form of Aeneas, Greek aineo 'to praise'. Hero of Virgil's Aeneid.
Jusuf: Bosnian and Balkan form of Yusuf, Arabic for Joseph, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Lita: Spanish diminutive of names ending in -lita, such as Carlita or Dolores. Also Latin 'joyful'.
Lubin: French, from Latin Leubinus, 'dear' from Germanic leub. Saint Lubin of Chartres.
Maira: Arabic Mayra, Irish Maire or Portuguese, a form of Mary, Hebrew origin.
Mame: Wolof, 'grandparent'. Common in Senegal; also a French familiar form of Mary.
